video_title: BREAKING NEWS: The Jazz Are Actually Good Again | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Utah Jazz are a legitimate playoff team for 2027
quotes.excerpt: I see a playoff team in the Jazz. I'm not talking about a play-in team.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: They mailed in the last couple of years. They tried to get Cooper Flagg, that didn't work. They tried even harder to get the number one overall pick, they got two, they got Darren Peterson, so mission accomplished. Along the way, they made some savvy deals that got real guys in there. You have Keyonte George now anchoring your front line. You just give Keyonte George a new contract extension. I look at that roster, I see a playoff team in the Jazz. I'm not talking about a play-in team. They have to go through the play-in to get there because I don't think they're a top-six team, but I see a team that is going to make the playoffs in 2027.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I would say that there's no way to possibly know. This is a team that is a mystery box if there ever was one. These guys largely haven't played together. We don't know what Darren Peterson is going to be.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Darren Peterson's potential as a starter alongside Keyonte George
quotes.excerpt: Darren Peterson slotted into that starting spot, playing opposite Keyonte George. Maybe that happens, maybe Ace Bailey.
quotes.quote: As I am looking at their depth chart, they have Darren Peterson slotted into that starting spot, playing opposite Keyonte George. Maybe that happens, maybe Ace Bailey gets that spot. There is the unknown, which is pretty obvious. Can George and Peterson coexist at a playoff level? Is Darren Peterson ready to play at that level? Typically, it is a lot harder for guards to assimilate to the NBA than it is wings and bigs. If you look historically, Peterson is a great player, maybe he is ready to shake off all that nonsense from Kansas last year, whatever it was. We will see if that works.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Hardy's challenge managing the Jazz's frontcourt rotation
quotes.excerpt: We know Jalen Jackson can play center sometimes, is not a center full-time, which could mean more time.
quotes.quote: How does Will Hardy work that front line? Because we know Jalen Jackson can play center sometimes, is not a center full-time, which could mean more time for Yusuf Nurkic, which could mean like that jumbo lineup that they may have to run out there with Lauri Markkanen. Now Lauri Markkanen has been a small forward before, he did it in Cleveland with the Cavaliers, but he has thrived and grown into an All-Star level player being a power forward, being a frontcourt type of guy. For long stretches you are going to need to play Jackson and Markkanen as your two bigs, I think, in that frontcourt, and maybe go smaller with Ace Bailey, Bryce Sensabaugh, guys like that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Will Hardy is a top-three coach of the year candidate
quotes.excerpt: I think he is going to be top-three coach of the year this year.
quotes.quote: Will Hardy, I think is the best coach with the crappiest record that is out there. I think he is a phenomenal X's and O's coach. I think this is going to be his opportunity to compete for a Coach of the Year spot. I think he might, I would go as far as to say he is going to be top-three Coach of the Year this year because I think the Jazz are going to be a playoff team, and if they are, he is going to get a lot of consideration for that.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Lauri Markkanen's limited games played due to injury management
quotes.excerpt: In the last couple years, he played 42 games and 47 games, 55 the year before.
quotes.quote: I was just trying to look up Lauri Markkanen's career stats. In the last couple years, he played 42 games and 47 games, 55 the year before, so still not close to 80. Obviously, a lot of that time he was not playing may have been the Utah Jazz being extremely careful about his injuries so as to protect their draft position. I am not blaming him or saying, oh, he is hurt all the time or anything. However, I would like to see him play.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Lauri Markkanen's health is critical to the Jazz's success
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Jackson is a stud, but they are going to need Lauri Markkanen to be a stud also.
quotes.quote: Jalen Jackson is a stud, but they are going to need Lauri Markkanen to be a stud also, and over the wear and tear of 82 games, can he keep up the level he did in that All-Star season? And can he, now we really do get to see what his health is like.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Houston's success depends on Kevin Durant and Fred VanVleet's health
quotes.excerpt: You are depending on Kevin Durant health, you are depending on Fred VanVleet health.
quotes.quote: I have seen people say, oh, Houston could be third in the West, which I think they could be, but you are depending on Kevin Durant health, you are depending on Fred VanVleet health, and I am not saying, and God knock on every surface because Fred is, that is another big question. What is going to happen with Fred? Is he going to get to play 80 games, you know, 78 games, or is it going to be, you know, still dealing with injuries?

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Concerns regarding Jason Tatum's health management
quotes.excerpt: I was incredibly impressed with his comeback last year. Obviously flagged a bit at the end.
quotes.quote: It is the same way I feel like with Jason Tatum. I was incredibly impressed with his comeback last year. Obviously flagged a bit at the end, and you just wonder how they are going to manage him this year.
